explicit_idempotency_policy: Each mutation explicitly declares whether it supports idempotent retries.
For supported operations, repeating a request with the same valid idempotency identity must not create duplicate business effects.
Do not assume every HTTP mutation is idempotent merely because its method normally suggests it.
Document key format, scope, retention, and behavior when a key is reused with a different request.
identity_and_request_binding: Bind an idempotency identity to the authenticated actor, operation, and appropriate resource/workspace scope.
Bind the identity to relevant request content so conflicting reuse can be rejected safely.
Repeated equivalent requests return the original logical outcome or a documented equivalent.
A request identity is not an audit-event identity and is never an authorization credential.
concurrency_and_recovery: Concurrent duplicate requests must not independently commit the same logical effect.
Define behavior for requests that are in progress, fail, time out, or are retried after a process restart.
Persist enough deduplication state to meet documented retention and recovery guarantees.
If a result is uncertain after interruption, resolve the committed outcome before executing the effect again.
Do not claim exactly-once delivery across system boundaries without supporting evidence.
unique_audit_and_effect_identity: Each committed logical effect requiring audit evidence has a unique, attributable effect/event identity.
Retries of the same logical effect must not create duplicate logical audit/activity events.
Distinct successful effects must not be collapsed merely because they share an actor or operation.
Audit records retain required actor, timestamp, event type, workspace/resource references, and safe details under Group 4.
Business state, deduplication outcome, and required audit evidence follow Group 10's consistency and recovery contract.
security_and_information_disclosure: Re-check current authentication, session validity, authorization, workspace scope, and resource relationships on protected requests.
A previously recorded idempotency key must not grant access after membership removal, role change, or session revocation.
Replayed outcomes must not disclose data the caller is no longer authorized to see.
Do not log credentials, tokens, or sensitive request content as deduplication evidence.
verification_obligations: Test repeated equivalent requests and conflicting reuse of the same key.
Test concurrent duplicate requests and requests racing with failures or restarts.
Verify one logical business effect and the required audit identity/evidence.
Test retries after lost acknowledgements and timeouts.
Verify deduplication retention and expiry behavior.
Test authorization changes before replay and confirm old keys cannot bypass access controls.
Trace results to canonical TaskFlow acceptance criteria and preserve independently verifiable evidence.
